text: Summer is here, and it has come in the form of Morgan's Pier. Brought to you by the folks at R5 productions, this place has taken up residence at the former location of Rock Lobster (ick) and Octo8 (double ick). Morgan's Pier is one of the most beautiful additions to the waterfront after Race Street Pier (which is adjacent to Morgan's Pier, incidentally). With its reclaimed wood siding and paneling, former cable spools as table tops, trees strewn with lights and an expansive outdoor dining space in clear view of the gorgeous Ben Franklin Bridge, the whole place (especially at night) is nearly magical. This place has such promise. Please, please stay as you are Morgan's Pier. I want you to succeed, but I want you to stay authentic, local and not get ANYWHERE near what Cavanaugh's River Deck is. Pretty Please? Right now, it's festive without being out of control, laid-back like a waterfront bar and restaurant should be, and not a scene. People are behaving themselves, there are no crazy drunks or out of control kids trying to fight and/or suck face in public. Right now, it's perfection - and I hope, pray, and keep my fingers crossed that it will stay that way. If it does, you know where you can find me for the rest of the summer: parked in one of the many high bar chairs that line the back of the Pier that face the bridge with a cool brew in my hands. There's a small restaurant menu I've yet had the pleasure to sample, but am looking forward to it, and with two bars at either end of the property, there's enough place (and great staff) to get yourself a drink (solid draft specials - local brewers especially well-presented) and belly up to the bar to get you what you need (for now). There's room for live music (a stage has been added on the right of the front of the property when you come in) that is also occupied by DJ (management note: please get good talent - we need good tunes, this is not a club, right?) One low note - are the bathrooms. Simply speaking: Gross. Layout, the stalls, the sinks - everything. I think this place got a full makeover, save the restrooms. Fail. If only they carried the lovely decor through to this space too - these spaces are just as important. Trust me. Either way, I'm cautiously optimistic, like I was about the Piazza, but that place let me down. Morgan's Pier, please, please, please don't disappoint. You're so purty and perfect just the way you are.

text: I went to Maoz for the first time on a Friday night, looking for a quick, cheap, filling meal before a night of drinking with girlfriends. When I walked in, I was pleasantly surprised to hear some of Montreal playing, HUGE bonus points. It was fairly clean in there, very bright and colorful. I liked that the menu was straight-forward and simple--falafels, whole wheat or white pita and simple as that. Loved the salad bar and that I could add what I wanted and how much but it was a little dirty, which lowered the ratings for me.There was some mixing of the toppings--which I got a little annoyed with, because some of the toppings are labeled gluten-free or vegan, cross contamination is no bueno. Their tahini, cilantro, and garlic sauces are great; they were out of tzaziki sauce, which I wanted to try, but maybe I'll try it next time. It was also a little busy when I went in and they only had a cook and someone at the register to handle all of the orders. It's a little clumsy how they deal with orders; everyone crowds around the counter/salad bar waiting for their pita, and while the rest of the order (mainly the fries) are still being cooked and everyone is hungrily packing their pitas full of awesome toppings, a line forms at the register, while the cashier is trying to wrap pitas and fries to go. All in all, the #2 Junior Meal Deal, a half sandwich with belgian fries and a drink was just what I wanted. Their whole wheat pita was alright, I would have appreciated if it was warmer (though I did take it to go). The falafels are really delicious, they're not super dense or overcooked--almost as good as homemade ones! The belgian fries were a nice surprise too, especially when dipped in their garlic sauce. I'll be back for more.

Soup, salad, a spring roll and a good sized entree. You won't leave hungry and you'll probably take some with you. The dinner menu is more extensive with a full section devoted to seafood. This is in addition to your appetizers, salads and soups, noodle dishes and curries, with chicken, beef, pork, tofu and all veggie options. My favorites are the yellow curry with chicken - medium is a great heat for this dish as it is sweet from the coconut milk base; pad thai - get this hot. Its amazing and has nice even mix of ingredients - you don't get overpowered with egg or tofu and your meat portion will be healthy. The garlic pepper entree is wonderful but I'd recommend skipping this if you aren't a big garlic fan. :) Last night we got take-out for New Years. As always, our food was ready lickety split in 20 minutes. We got vegetarian spring rolls, yellow curry with chicken and the pad ped with beef (bamboo shoots, green beans, bell peppers and basil). Medium was plenty spicy and we easily had leftovers despite the fact it was all going down quickly with the help of a beautiful bottle of sparkling Domaine Carneros Rose. Our take out order ran us $32 which we gladly paid. If you've never tried this place, do so. You won't regret it.

text: This was my first, and last, visit to this Nashville restaurant. My food basically had no flavor. It really seemed like the chefs had lost/were out of all of their spices, including simple salt and pepper. The broccoli had no flavor, the cheese had no flavor, the garlic ranch salad dressing might as well have been water, because it had absolutely no flavor whatsover. The BBQ sauce was the most flavorful thing on my plate, and it was a bit too sweet for my taste. My husband's chicken tenders were similarly without flavor, but he did enjoy his ribs and fries. We also ordered the White Chocolate Banana Cream Pie to split for dessert. It was just ok. The graham cracker crust was good, but the pie itself was, much like the rest of the food here, rather flavorless. Most times, I believe in the "3 strikes, you're out" policy, but with Rafferty's, I'm afraid it's 2 strikes and never returning. We could have gone just about anywhere and have gotten a much more flavorful meal for less money than we paid here.

They've even kept the 1950's and early 1960's jukebox pop music which seems strange. We decided to order from their all day breakfast menu. Michael chose an omelet with potatoes and English muffin while I chose the Buttermilk hoecakes (although they are actually pancakes) with a side of bacon. The food was mediocre. Michael's omelet was barely warm and the cheese he asked for had just been melted over the top then allowed to sit so long it had firmed up again and congealed. Yes, service was slow and undoubtedly that part of the order was sitting in the window. His potatoes were OK although nothing particularly noteworthy. On my end the pancakes were a bit bland. Since I am currently dieting I decided to forgo the syrup and just use a little butter. While they were not inedible by any means they just didn't seem to be quite worth the hefty $6.95 price tag for three pancakes alone. The bacon, however, was tasty and high quality and prepared just as I had ordered it. The people seem genuinely friendly for the most part. Our server was a very nice older lady although I don't think waiting tables is really the career for her. While pleasant, she was rather inefficient and prone to forgetting simple things. It's also rude of a server to stand over the patron while they are filling out the charge slip and calculating the tip. This is one of those restaurants that seems just on the edge. With a little more attention to the food, some makeover in the decor, and a bit more efficiency in the front of the house and the kitchen it could succeed. However, without those things I'm not sure of the longevity of this business. Normally, in our neighborhood a new opening means a fairly full house for at least a few weeks. Later that month the AC started leaking and flooded our hallway. We called and told them about it and the super stopped the leak. The following day it leaked again and flooded our already damp apartment. There was now wall damage to go along with it. They finally called professional help eventually and fixed up the AC business and then cleaned up our carpet and all. This is not the end of the water damage. So I'm studying for an exam I have and I hear droplets in my roommates room. On my way to his room I step in damp hallway carpet yet again. I called them and they came and said that it was the girls upstairs who left their faucet on. OK, whatever the reason was that is completely unacceptable piping/structure of two stories. text: Warning...don't go here if you're in a hurry! It may seem like a great place to grab a quick bite to eat from the outside, considering they serve things like salads, sandwiches, and burgers. Not that the service is BAD...but they just seem to take a really long time making pretty basic food. I used to order the grilled cheese because it was pretty much the only vegetarian thing on the menu besides salads, but it's just meh. It always came pretty dry, not at all crispy or cooked very much, and not overly cheesy or melty. So I started just ordering fried foods, which are excellent as far as fried foods go, and with ranch. Their ranch has that buttermilky, homemade taste-the type that I could eat like soup (and probably would if no one else was around!). The mozzarella sticks are crisp, cheesy goodness, the fries have a little skin on them and seem fresh cut, which is a refreshing change from most places, and the fried pickles, which are a special currently, are huge dill spears covered in delicious breading, and heavenly dipped in ranch! But the real winner comes when ordering dessert! The ice cream at this place is flown in from Wisconsin, and it is incredible! We actually have it at dinner parties because it is THAT good. I recommend the cookie dough and mackinac island fudge. I often get a quart to go, because eating one or two scoops is never enough. They have other desserts too, including several specialized sundaes, and floats, but I never have room for those because my entire meal comes from the deep fryer. They sound tasty though. Again, this is a great place to bring the kids, to grab dessert, or to indulge in something fried, but if you actually have places to go and things to do, or you want to eat something a little healthier, I'd go elsewhere.

text: I signed up for the mobile service and was given a USB modem. I thought it would be great to be able to use it on the go and since I live a few blocks from the store, I'd be in the network range for good connectivity, but that hasn't been the case. When the service actually works, it works well. I can stream without long buffering times. The problem is that 2-3 times a week I'm on the phone with them getting the service up and running. They tell me there are two towers close to my house (I'm in Queen Village, bf is in Pennsport, it doesn't work in either neighborhood), but for some reason I have constant trouble connecting to them. When I call they tell me they have to "reset the modem" and then the service works. I've never been able to get the modem to work outside my neighborhood and although there are other cities that are supposed to have clear service, I've never been able to get the modem to work (I've tried Fort Lauderdale, Chicago, Baltimore and San Francisco. I don't even bother bringing it with me anymore). Before you sign up for the service, make sure you're in a city center - the 'burbs are typically out of their range. Now, living close to a clear store, I thought I could take the modem in and have them fix the problem, however, the store is not able to do anything but sell the devices. They can't change your billing, they can't address connectivity issues and they pretty much can't help you once you've signed up for the service. They just refer you to the clear customer service line. The customer service line connects you to a call center somewhere in Asia where they barely speak english and aren't going to be able to assist you with much. I've been given the following advice when I've called: move to another room in your house, make sure you don't have double-paned or tinted windows, make sure the modem is at least 4 feet off the ground. Also they've told me more than once that the towers are down and I would have to just wait until they sent a technician out to fix them which could take up to 5 days (it actually has taken up to 3). Unfortunately I'm locked into a contract, but after a few months of this, I might just cut my losses and try to buy out of it.

text: My wife and I went to Sears in the Moorestown Mall, NJ on Memorial Day to purchase the Weber Genesis Espresso Porcelain Enamel 3-Burner Gas Grill and some accessories. As a courtesy to Sears, to whom I frequent on a regular basis, I will give you some advice on how to teach your employees proper customer service: 1) When a customer tells what they want, drop your sales pitch and stop trying to move merchandise they are not interested in. Focus on the item they are interested in and get the sale. Your personal preference might be Kenmore grills and it might be a fine product, but it's not what we wanted. My family swears by Weber and we did our research in advance and knew exactly what we wanted...all you had to do was tell us about the financing options and/or available discounts, simple 2) Be professional. This includes no arguing with the customers that disagree with your opinion, do not raise your voice at women, and stop saying "OK" after every sentence as if we don't understand what you're saying. How we got into a debate over stainless steel grates and porcelain coated cast iron grates is beyond me 3) Know your merchandise. As my wife mentioned during our mini-debate, you were the first salesperson to ever tell us that stainless steel grates are better than porcelain enameled cast iron. Such a general statement to throw out! There are benefits to both, but you only focused on the benefits of stainless steel because you were trying to move Kenmore merchandise. This throws up a red flag for informed buyers. You made it clear that you read reviews on the Sears website, which is fine, but I read reviews from multiple website. Why don't you read the below link and learn a thing or two about the benefits of both so that you can properly inform your customers: http://www.ehow.com/info_10052854_stainless-steel-vs-porcelain-grill-cooking-surfaces.html 4) Do not lie to customers - It's amazing how every salesman worked for the competition at one point in their lives so you know more than the "average buyer". I found it convenient that you once sold Weber products only. When I hear this, I shut everything else out that you say, especially when I feel like you're just trying to move merchandise 5) Don't carry merchandise if you're not interested in selling it. You mocked us when we said we would spend $700.00 on a Weber grill vs. a much bigger stainless steel Kenmore grill. You probably don't have any say in what merchandise your store carries, but maybe your know-it-all arrogant attitude will work on your managers As I said before, I'm a loyal Sears's customer so I won't let one "bad egg" ruin my perception of Sears, but I refused to give this guy any commission. text: Old Peking offers workmanlike renditions of Szechuan standards which would have made Mao proud. The Singapore noodles caught my eye because of the singular asterisk warning of spice (the only one on the page) and the wok-fried concoction of angel-hair thin rice noodles, fried pork, egg, and shrimp with veggies and a hot curry sauce is worth a try. We still had to request spicy pepper sauce on the side, but the dish does warm the soul. The bbq beef lo mein is sweet and plentiful, the egg flower soup thicker than most, and the servers are knowledgeable and fast. The ambience is stricly commie cafeteria and beyond non-descript, but more than half the diners are Asian (a tacit endorsement) and nary a parking space was to be had on a Sunday night. text: My experience with Harmony Mental Health Services was a disheartening one that made me feel insignificant and anonymous. Dealing with longtime depression and anxiety, I went to Harmony to see a psychiatrist. I was first put through a mandatory intake process with Dr. Cheryl Bork Hadley, who demonstrated the worst listening skills I have ever encountered in a therapist. She interrupted every sentence I started. Literally. I never obtained a real opportunity to be heard. She spoke of cursory topics and made jokes in poor taste when I was clearly in an overwhelmed and vulnerable state which did not invite this type of conversation. I left the office with permission to see a psychiatrist and feeling worse than I had when I went in. Dr. Monheit prescribed medication for two weeks, a trial. I was on my lunch break from work--since he is only in the office one day out of the week--and waited 45 minutes to be seen. The appointment lasted less than ten minutes. At the follow up a few weeks later (after I'd run out of medication because he moved our appointment), he asked generally how I was doing (the only question he asked me the entire appointment). I responded that I hadn't felt anything from the medication yet, which made sense, since he'd said himself that it takes four to six weeks to take effect. (So should it not have been prescribed for more than two weeks?) Instead of asking more specific questions, he responded by asking me if I wanted to try another drug for the next month. He poses it as my choice, yet provides no guidelines of what to consider. A buffet of drugs. A merry-go-round. He gave no explanation of the medication, no background, and no reasoning why he was prescribing it when taking my circumstantial and historical factors into account. Those factors were never brought up. It was as if he'd pulled the name of the drug out of thin air. I felt completely anonymous. No conversation. I understand fully that each patient reacts uniquely to a medication, and that results can't be known until the medication is taken. I do not seek a seer out of a psychiatrist. I do, however, need communication and the sense that the consultant is taking all factors into consideration. When I asked about things I should consider when deciding whether to take a medication or not, he gave no offers. He gave me two minutes--literally--to decide. He clearly wanted to get me out of the door with as little investigation as possible. The appointment lasted 6 minutes. Patients deserve more than the rip of an Rx slip after a single question asked. I will not go back to Harmony, having wasted time, money and trust.
label: NEG

text: I've tried and I've tried, but after four trips to this location I've never actually managed to eat one of their burgers. I'll start with their hours of business. I know it is a downtown location, but two of my four trips to try Monkey Burger have ended in after hours disappointment. On most weekdays they are closed by 3:30 PM, causing my 5:30 PM burger craving to go unanswered. On my second trip to Monkey Burger, I learned they are not open at all on Sundays. I feel like those of us who work normal hours, but don't work downtown are just being left out of the Monkey Burger experience. Despite their inconvenient hours, I kept trying. Last night the stars aligned, and thanks to Second Saturdays I made it to Monkey Burger while they were actually open. My girlfriend and I walked in around 8:00 PM, and upon entering it isn't really clear how you put in your order. My girlfriend and I took the safe bet, and had a seat at the bar. A few minutes passed, and not one employee had interacted with us at all in that time. When a group of three people, who had already placed their order, started getting free samples of beer from the bartender, we decided to leave. We walked around downtown for a while, tried some food from the street vendors, and eventually decided to give Monkey Burger yet another try. It was a few minutes after 9:00 PM this time, and we again took two seats at the bar. We were almost immediately asked to move to a table. We politely obliged, and moved to one of three empty tables directly in front of the bar. None of these tables had been cleaned yet. A busser came and cleaned a table near ours and then left. A few minutes later the busser returned to clean a different table, and then left. We decided to switch to a clean table, only to have the busser immediately come out and clean the table we had just been sitting at. By this point it was 9:20 PM, and still no one had made any attempt to take our order. After a couple of minutes, we went up to the register and asked if we could get some service. There were three employees near the register when we walked up. The first one mumbled something, put his finger up, and walked away without ever making eye contact. The second employee looked at the floor, and immediately turned his back on us. The third employee had no choice but to talk to us. He walked up to the register and said, "I guess I can try to help you." We told the unlucky employee, who hadn't been as quick to leave as his coworkers, that we would like to place an order. He informed us that they were only serving beer and sides, because they were out of burgers. Looking around, everyone else had burgers. Including some people at the bar who had just got their burgers! The guy behind the register made no attempt to sympathize with our situation, and instead just said, "We had a busy night," in an annoyed tone of voice. He stood there in silence, blinking for a moment before we just turned to walk out of Monkey Burger. It was only 9:20 PM, and despite not closing until 10:30 on this particular day, they had run out of everything on their menu. After leaving Monkey Burger, we walked down to El Charro Cafe. Despite arriving five minutes before they closed, the service staff at El Charro was very happy to seat us, and provided us with both excellent service and food. El Charro went above and beyond, where as Monkey Burger wouldn't even try. Maybe I'm old fashioned, but when I go out to eat I expect: - to be treated like I exist, instead of being ignored - not to be treated like I'm bothering the employees - and to actually expect to get some food I've been treated better at McDonald's than Monkey Burger, and McDonald's hours are more convenient. Monkey Burger has terrible customer service, and that's all I can say about them.
label: NEG

When that didn't faze me, he explained that they didn't like them because Costco charges $80 for $100 worth of gift certificates, so they lose $20. I hadn't even been aware that they were purchased at Costco and I don't care. My wife, who loves to sign up for newsletters, pointed out that Ric's Grill is offering a deal through bookatable.ca, which the manager informed us is owned by Ric's Grill, where you can buy a $75 gift certificate for $40. They're losing nearly half there, so they're worried about a measly $10 on a $50 gift certificate? And it's not like we only have gone there with gift certificates or spend only what our gift certificate will cover. It's also short-sighted because we've always said nice things about Ric's Grill. We like the downtown location, the food has always been good and the service, not bad. Are we likely to say anything nice now or go back? Yeah, right. We're going to tell everyone our story. Great business plan there guys. If your restaurant is going to participate in a gift certificate deal with a store like Costco, don't play games and have stores opt out because they're afraid of losing a bit in the deal. When businesses start arguing over these kinds of things it makes me wonder how long they're going to be around. I'm really not impressed.

text: Ok, any of my friends know I love this place. Let's get one thing out of the way - it's not the cheapest place to eat in town, generally when the wife and I go here and eat, by the time we're done (cocktails, share appetizer, 2 entrees, bottle of wine, desert) we are in the $150-$200 range. But let me tell you - it's *so* worth it. Plus, you can totally eat there for a lot less than that and you can even order food at the bar if you're in a pinch. We started going to LuLou's probably 6-7 years ago (or more?) and I fell in love with this place from day one. At that time I didn't know a place like this existed in Reno. At that time both the husband and wife team that own the restaurant were there with Colleen working the front of the house and Troy running the kitchen. They were doing amazing dishes and had fantastic service. Then a few years ago Troy got hired as the Executive Chef at the Eldorado and there was a period where it wasn't the same 'LuLou's' experience and the food wasn't quite as good. That said however, for the past 2 years or so they are back on their game and frankly, better than ever. The food coming out of the kitchen is top notch, if you go while Farmers Markets are happening you'll find plenty of ingredients from that including the heirloom tomatoes which are awesome. I think we've yet to find a dish we didn't like at LuLous - their salads are great, especially the 'hearts of romaine' and butterleaf lettuce. One of my favorite entrees is their Ribeye that is served with swiss chard and skinny fries. The steak (I enjoy medium rare) is perfectly cooked and has SO much flavor. The swiss chard, which is a side comes in a little cast iron pot and tastes amazing (enough so that I wish they'd serve it as a separate dish). The skinny fries are amazing and usually anyone else at the table is always grabbing them off my plate - they taste so good! I've tried a lot of their other entrees which are all excellent but that ribeye has to be my favorite. Another MAJOR part of my LuLou's experience is the service. It's top notch. The servers are always friendly and attentive and it's nice to see the same faces when you come back to the restaurant. I'll specifically call out Steve that works there as the man - always goes the extra mile to make sure you have a good experience there (you can request a table in his section if you call ahead/reservations). Personally, I feel that this is one of the, if not the, best places to eat in Reno if you're looking for a fine dining experience. Don't bother bringing your own wine as the corkage is high but the prices are reasonable and the selection is great (some stuff I haven't been able to find locally). Also, please go with the expectation that it's not cheap and that you're going to pay a fair amount for a good meal. Most of the time when I talk to someone that doesn't like LuLou's it always gets back to the fact that they didn't want to spend that much. To enjoy this restaurant - If it's not in your budget, don't go. Lastly, if you're going for a special reason (birthday, etc.) then let them know when you make a reservation and they will go the extra mile.

The ambiance in here is sick, may even be enough of a reason by itself to go -Service is definitely on point (if not a little snooty, but what would you expect at a high end restaurant?) -The food is excellent. For appetizer, I got the dobin mushi soup, which was pretty good but mostly just broth for $10, and a spicy salmon roll, which IMO, is the best roll of sushi anywhere! For dinner, I went with the angry chicken. The chicken was melt in you mouth good, especially with the sauce it went with, although it wasn't exactly spicy, and for $27 I would have expected a side dish to go with it. For appetizer, my fiancé got a spicy vegetable tempura roll, which she seemed to really enjoy. For dinner they, were awesome enough to make here a vegetarian version of the ishi yoki bop with tofu, of which even I thoroughly enjoyed, and we also shared a side of the sake butter sautéed japanese mushrooms. All in all, we both had an awesome meal which we won't soon forget. - The "icing on the cake" of our meal, however, was the most incredible ice cream ever, which was some sort of sake coffee type of ice cream. Hard to really describe, but trust me its worth every penny and every calorie! On the downside: -Whether or not you come in with the understanding that its expensive, it still tends to bite you in the ass. What bothered me a little bit was the fact that some of the things were unnecessarily overpriced: for example, I ordered the "Sapporo Premium" beer for $7 and expected to be some kind of gourmet beer, but in actuality was just regular old Sapporo. -At first, our waitress did seem to have a sort of snideness or edge to her, but her attitude did improve throughout the evening. That's about it. I'd recommend coming here for a special occasion, but either way come knowing its gonna cost you!
label: POS

text: I tried this service and am very disappointed. They let me down. PROS: - TruGreen is the big brand; - They were servicing several of my neighbors' lawns. I used TruGreen on my lawn when I lived in Atlanta and it worked well. But this time, it was very poor. I prepaid for the while year - April - December, including a Fall aerate & over-seed service. For my lawn size, it was $475. Before I committed, I specifically asked about their ability to kill crab grass. I was assured they would kill it. So I took the plunge. They did ONE lawn treatment (supposedly - all I could show for it was the little lawn sign...) then buggered off. I did, however, get an invoice for the first service...even though I had PREPAID. So I called them. They use a giant, national call center, so it was 15 minutes on hold. (Great, personalized, local service!!!) They told me, "yeah, well, our system just DOES that. Just throw the invoice away..." Great. Very buttoned down and confidence-inspiring! About five weeks later, I saw a new sign at my neighbor's house, but none for me. I gave them the benefit of the doubt and waited another couple of weeks. Nothing. When I called them, they said, "oh, yeah, I see... Not sure why we skipped you... We'll get back out there as soon as we can." This is unacceptable, especially after I prepaid. As of now (mid-July) I have TONS OF CRABGRASS. So I had to fire them and get a refund for the balance. Unfortunately, I did have to pay for two, worthless "services." Never again. I just think this business model is poor: - The most experienced lawn people they have are their sales folks (of course). - The "customer service" person you get as a paid customer is a very basic phone-answerer who knows zero about lawn care. - Their automated phone system says "If you're interested in becoming a customer, press 1. She proceeded to tell me that I had to pay $350 upfront for a circumcision if we had a boy and that if it was a girl, we would be reimbursed. Needless to say, I was not expecting this since this was not on my initial paperwork and I knew my insurance covered circumcision 100% with no deductible. I called my insurance company to verify and indeed I should not have to pay for a covered expense upfront as a cash paying patient would. I explained my insurance to the receptionist and she absolutely did not care what my insurance was and said I had to pay it or take it up with Theresa Knight, MD. It just so happened, I was not scheduled to see Dr. Eastep, I was scheduled to see Theresa Knight, MD who is the owner of the practice. She came into the room with an attitude and asked what I was unhappy about. I filled her in and she said that she had not been paid for circumcisions since they are considered cosmetic and I had to pay $350 upfront. I questioned if this was following the agreement she signed with United Health Care. This really set her off and she told me to find another doctor's office. Needless to say, I was stunned since I was in the middle of a high risk pregnancy and I absolutely adore Dr. Eastep. I told her I wanted to talk with Dr Eastep prior to making any decisions and she said that would not be possible. I contacted my insurance company about this office policy and also sent my insurance company the paper work indicating I had to pay $350 upfront for a circumcision. My insurance company contacted WHS to let them know this was a violation of the contract. Theresa Knight, MD then wrote me a letter stating that all my appointments had been canceled and I needed to find a new OB-GYN. By the time I received the letter, we had already decided that it was in the best interest of our baby not to take the chance of Theresa Knight, MD delivering then performing a circumcision, if a boy. She showed her true, unprofessional colors and we would never take the chance of putting our baby's care in the hands of someone with her mercenary approach to medicine. When I found WHS on line, the website boasted about Theresa Knight being the CEO. I did not think anything bad about this at all, but now I know differently. She is more concerned with collecting money, even if it is a violation of the contract she has with an insurance company and the patient has full coverage than patient care. Let me reiterate, Dr Eastep is the most caring doctor I have ever seen in all my life! She is absolutely an amazing person and I would recommend her to anyone if she were not in this practice. My issue is with Theresa Knight, MD and the unethical office policies she has put in place. Proceed with caution!

Despite this, I have to say I did enjoy the food served up by Maya's - the tuna tar tar, the ceviche, the crab-shrimp-avocado-mango stack, and especially the soft-shell crab. We should have made a beeline for another restaurant as we noticed garbage being pelted out of the apartments directly above the restaurant onto the sidewalk in front of the restaurant, and even fireworks that were hurled at other dining patrons. After our drinks were brought to us (and sans glass for my boyfriend's Guinness) we asked to move to another table that was not within the line of fire, we were told we would have to pay for our beers and tip before moving to another table because the waitress did not cover the table that was DIRECTLY DIAGONAL from ours. The restaurant was not that empty and it seemed there were only two of them working the area. We chose to remain in our original seats and take our chances (again dismissing another red flag). My boyfriend ordered a spider roll, that was not only in the shape of a rectangle, making it a sushi cube, but consisted mainly of rice and little to no crab. My crab salad was literally lump crab from a can atop a bed of cold glass noodles on top of lettuce. Without seasoning or taste. My beef satay was made up of chunks of undercooked meat accompanied by a runny, oily peanut sauce. Although starving from a night of revelry, I couldn't stomach the tasteless food and we called it a night. The cherry on top of this disastrous sundae - our fortunes cookies, whose messages seem to have been created in the most oddball fortune cookie factory on earth. Mine read - "You would prosper in the field of wacky inventions", my boyfriend's - "You constantly struggle for self improvement - and it shows". Huh??? From literal start to finish, the most disappointing dinner experience for (a) a person of Chinese descent, (b) from NY, (c) who is a foodie and indulges in all types of cuisine regularly at all price points, (d) who has just been to China and experienced real Chinese food. The after effects of this dining debacle were felt by both of us the next morning as we took turns in the bathroom before commencing on our 2 hour journey back to New York. If I could give this place zero stars I would. Avoid this place at all costs...

The rest of the menu looked quite tasty (gourmet breakfast fare, the scents of BBQ wafting through the restaurant and the huge sandwiches and burgers delivered to wide-eyed patrons all around us). The Fat Hen omelet was also a smashing success, with a delicious flaky biscuit and homemade jam. The diversity of the menu will bring me back, along with an above-par experience dining at the counter. Fat Hen is a popular and there will be a wait on weekends. text: Stopped into Mena's for lunch today. I should preface my review by saying this was not our original destination, but the pizza place we were looking for was closed. Regrettably, this table was literally in the doorway at the front of the restaurant. If you opened the left door to enter the restaurant, you would run smack-dab into our table. But I digress. It took several minutes for a waitress to bring menus and silverware. The menu is posted outside, so there were no suprises as I reviewed the menu. I decided to go with the meatball po boy for lunch ($7.00). Our food arrived after approx. 15 minutes. That doesn't seem like long to have to wait, except for the fact that a party that came in five minutes after us, received their food first. On to the food. The po boy was good. The bread was nothing special, but the meatballs were tasty. That was about it. The service is really what killed this visit. One member of our party had asked for mayo on the side of her po boy and they forgot it. It took our waitress more than five minutes to return with the mayo. We also never had our drinks refilled. And when we asked for receipts from our meal, only one of the three people received their receipt. We had to catch the eye of another waitress in the kitchen who sent someone out to investigate. It's unfortunate. Too many other good options in NO though to dwell on this. I won't be back.
label: NEG

text: Drinks: 5 stars Food: 2 1/2 I don't know about this one, I could have easily given it a 3 star but the drinks we had were very good. Unfortunately, the food was just kinda meh. The tater tots ($5) were not really anything special and the Goat Cheese balls ($7), while above average in flavor, didn't seem to live up to the hype and pretension that permeates this place. Now, I'm all for a little bit of pretension and exclusivity now and then, but next time I visit this place (and btw, this is where you should START your evening) I'll sit at the bar and have a great cocktail or two. As for my drink, the Eclipse ($12) the drink had a complex flavor comprised of Flor de Cana 7 yr Rum, demerara syrup, averna, and chocolate bitters. There was also an orange peel which made for a wonderful drink that was complimented by their somewhat signature ice ball. (Tip: if you want to make these at home, you can buy molds online. I bought mine from the SF art museum of all places. Spherical Ice Mold: http://bit.ly/tpH2Yn $16) Another interesting thing our server Nicole stated was that the drinks become more intense the father down the list. So, mine was fairly strong as it was third of four on the Rum drink list. The other drinks in my group included the Dark & Stormy ($12), and the Bacon Old Fashioned ($12). Both tasted great.

text: Kooky Cocunut rocks! I try to stop by here every time I'm driving through Indian Rocks Beach. KC is located in a tiny building right on the corner of Gulf Blvd and 8th St. It's small enough that it's easy to miss if your not looking closely. But you won't want to miss it, as KC serves up a great mix of ice cream, sandwiches and treats, all in a classic setting of "funky Florida beach shack". Inside are only about 3 small tables, but there are plenty of picnic tables outside if the weather is nice. The beach is only a short walk away, and they even have their own chairs there that you can use for a short while during your visit. Nothing better than catching some rays and waves while enjoying your refreshments. All the staff I've met have been extraordinary friendly, and unless it's busy, are more than happy to chat and give you recommendations for anything you need in the area. They're also on Facebook (http://www.facebook.com/pages/Kooky-Coconut/109508104883) and Twitter (http://twitter.com/#!/KookyCoconut), so you can stay connected and catch an occasional deal for their fans. Everything I've had here has been very good, especially the ice cream and their Island Cuban sandwich, their twist on the classic hot-pressed Cuban. As much as I like many of the well-made classic versions around Tampa, this sandwich stands up just fine to them for flavor and tasty goodness. They also have a good choice of cold beverages for those hot beach days, too. Prices are good for the quality. On a "classic beach shack" scale, I give Kooky Coconut: Atmosphere: 5 for it's classic beach shack vibe Service: 5 Food: 5 Value: 4 Note: Kooky Coconut has some prime parking in their lot available for their guests, considering the lack of street parking in the area and how heavily it's used by beachgoers. So during busy times, their staff police their parking lot strictly. If you pull in to park you may be approached to let you know it's their exclusive lot. They're not trying to be unfriendly, they're just trying to keep from towing folks that take up a valuable parking space for their day at the beach.
label: POS

text: Seems they don't appreciate customer complaints I had a VERY unpleasant experience at this Arch street location of Fuel. Called to complain about it but they never followed up...despite the fact that I explicitly requested to speak with the owner directly. About one month ago, my wife and I decided to take advantage of the $10 for $20 groupon that was going on for that particular day. We'd only eaten at Fuel one other time in the past and that was at the Walnut street location. We thought it was good so we decided to buy the groupon. This Fuel location was closer to where we live so we figured it would be nice if they were just as good as the Walnut location. We arrived there in the early evening hours. When we got there, it was not busy at all and there were no customers in the store. A young lady and guy were working the counter. As we were looking at the menu, they were obviously preoccupied with a phone call. We finally decided on what we wanted and patiently waited for them to finish the call. It appeared as if they were taking a large order from someone. While the guy took the order on the phone, the young lady punched it into the computer screen to generate the sale. At least, that's how it appeared to the both of us. For about 5-10 minutes we stood there as they conversed on the phone. All of a sudden, the guy starts laughing. Best I could tell, it was a friend of his, playing a joke on him, acting like he was ordering a LOT of food, just to get a rise out of them. Up to this point, I'm actually not bothered at all. I've worked in retail before. It can be bland at times and a friend calling on the phone lightens up the day. What bothered me was what happened next. Suddenly, a slew of curse words flowed out of this guy's mouth as if he were sitting in his living room. "F you you F'in A-hole...hahahaha" He must have dropped the F bomb about 5 times and threw in several other choice curse words. I couldn't believe what I was hearing!!!!! "You F'in B**ch! Hahaha!!" How in the world could an employee talk like that in front of customers!!!??? Not only was he cursing non-stop, he was practically yelling them as well!! I couldn't believe my ears!!! I was completely turned off and despite the fact that I NEVER complain, I knew I had to call about this one. It was completely unacceptable. So, the following Monday or Tuesday, I called to speak with the owner to do just that. When I called, a very nice woman answered and explained that the owner of the store wasn't in. Apparently, his name is Rocco. She identified herself as Shannon and told me that she could take the complaint and relay it to him. I asked her what her job title was and she said she was a key holder and a supervisor. Reluctantly, I explained everything to her and described in detail the guy I was complaining about. I even asked her if she knew whom I was talking about and she said that she knew exactly the person I was referring to. I actually had no problems with the young lady that was working the counter that day. Now, while I was talking to Shannon, part of me had the suspicion that I just might be calling and talking to the lady that was there the same day that my wife and I visited. So, I told her that I wanted my complaint to be followed up with by Rocco, the owner. She had no problem with that. I told her that I was unavailable until Friday so if he could call me then, I would appreciate it. She told me that wasn't a problem, she apologized for my experience, and that was the end of the call. Well, that was two weeks ago! Still no call from the owner!! Should I call and say, "Hey, you guys never called me back?" You know, I really don't think I should have to do that. I called and was calm and mature about my horrible experience but I obviously didn't express how turned off I was to this Fuel location. Either that or they just didn't think it was important enough. Truly unbelievable!! I will NEVER, EVER eat at this Fuel location again, and I'll be sure to tell my friends about it as well!

text: Oh boy, here it goes. Before reading further, I want to express how much I enjoyed the lunch specials and dinner menu for the Mandarin food. This review, however, is for the dim sum/AYCE portion of the restaurant - which, in all honesty, I don't even know why they bother offering. It was so awful, they're just doing a disservice to themselves. When we sat down, there were three other people at the bar and one sushi chef. We arrived during lunch hour and the whole place - sushi area AND restaurant area - was dead. I didn't mind because it's a Monday and I've been to the restaurant portion before when it was jam-packed AND empty, and it was always delicious food. Unfortunately, I was wrong to think that an empty sushi part of the restaurant was okay. Firstly, we sat at a booth, which always makes me feel like I'm not getting as quick or as good of service (but they were dead, so we were the only table to help). There were four adults, three of which were AYCE lunch, and one toddler - we were brought waters, and they didn't bring ANYTHING for the toddler in our group, or even offer. In fact, I don't recall them ever actually asking WHAT we wanted to drink, just bringing water and moving on to food. I'm a bit of a pain when it comes to ordering sushi from a booth because I can't share a massive plate with everyone else - it grosses me out. He humored me, though, and brought an additional marking menu for me to make separate orders. The person in the group ordering Mandarin food ordered way before anyone else, then the pair across the table from us ordered on their sushi menu, and finally my marked menu was taken. Again, they didn't ask if we were ordering anything for the toddler... I suppose they just assumed she'd be sharing with us, which we ended up doing, so it worked out. I'm just a little perturbed by the complete lack of acknowledgment for the toddler altogether; in any other restaurant, people ask what the child will be drinking or eating, etc etc. I'm upset about all of this, and she's not even my kid! The Mandarin food came out way before any of the sushi. I'd say she was eating for about seven or even ten minutes before we finally got any of our sushi. The pair that ordered together got their massive plate, which seemed to be missing a few things that one of the two had ordered - and, finally, mine came out... to my surprise, it was covered in items I did NOT order, and neither did the other people eating AYCE. Just...random sushi rolls that had almost nothing to do with what I wanted off of the menu. AND THE TASTE?! I couldn't even tell you what kind of fish was in each roll, because they all tasted EXACTLY the same. The rice was so over powered by the vinegar that each roll tasted sour and tangy - and not in a good way. The scallops were mushy and soggy, and almost like dissolving scallop 'goop'. I ordered five hand rolls and only two long rolls (I hadn't eaten at all yet today at that point), and I'm pretty sure I got SIX long rolls. text: Visited on Thursday, October 4th with a reservation for 6:45pm. BF and I arrived early and they were able to immediately accommodate us with a table. I ordered the petite filet rare, which prompted the waitress to ask me, "Cool and pink in the center, right?" When I waited tables, I always had to ask the same thing, which boggled my mind that people didn't know what the difference between rare, med rare, med, med well, and well are. I learned that if I didn't ask, people would get so upset at me when they received their meat, not knowing that well-done typically means you need a band saw to slice through it. When I got my steak, it was very medium inside. It was medium well on the edges, and a warm faint pink in the middle....definitely NOT rare. I was pretty disappointed that a place that charges $38.95 for a teeny piece of steak could screw up the temperature, but I ate it anyway, because I didn't want to see it go to waste, and medium wasn't going to kill me. Personally, if you're going to ask for a filet cooked anything more than medium rare, you might as well not even order a nice cut of meat. BF ordered the BBQ Scottish Salmon Filet which was on top of a slow roasted mushroom salad. It was presented very nicely and, since I am partial to mushrooms, loved the salad. The two sides we shared were the macaroni and cheese (TO DIE FOR) and the string beans which were absolutely delicious. The atmosphere is very nice, but if you want something intimate, ask to sit farther away from the bar area, the suits can get a little rowdy once they loosen their ties. :) I enjoyed my meal immensely, and hope to be back soon. One little mis-cooked steak is not going to keep me away from their mac and cheese!!!!

Monica did everything -- food, decorations and service -- in a way that perfectly fit our needs. Our overriding goal was for all guests to feel loved and valued, and to be glad they were part of our special occasion. Our standards were high -- and wonderful, plentiful, somewhat sophisticated food served in an elegant but friendly atmosphere was very important to us. We could not have been more pleased! Monica was wonderful to work with from the very beginning. She listened to us and understood what we wanted. She suggested a brunch buffet instead of a dinner, since that would provide high quality food in a budget friendly way. She then gave us several menus from which to choose. In addition, she guided us through decorations, including the many choices that must be made for linens and dinnerware, and flowers. She was there from early morning on, coordinating the event so that we did not have to worry, and was present during the whole reception -- making it look as though we knew what we were doing. :-) She is wonderfully talented and experienced -- and made it possible for us achieve the reception of our dreams in the best possible way. Weddings are complicated and emotional events; highly skilled professionals are a must. Monica came highly recommended by friends who are very knowledgeable about Nashville events and resources. Her services and food are a bit costly, but we feel that we got a bargain -- far more beautiful and delicious and well coordinated than we dreamed possible.

text: I think I found my new best restaurant in Philadelphia. I was blown away by this place. I've been reading about it for some time and had the opportunity to go with my mutually food loving mother when she was in town. We were seated right away in the upstairs room that has nice big windows looking down onto Walnut St and a cool grey, modern polished look. There is a wine station in the middle of the big room. The tables along the walls are a little close together, as evidenced by the woman who spilled some food on the guy next to her as she was leaving. We also happened to be sitting between two groups that were having the most pretentious conversations while wining and dining their mistresses, but I will not blame the restaurant for the crowd they attract. Every single bite of food I put in my mouth blew my mind. This was hands down the best meal I've had in quite a while. We shared a few appetizers: the cremini mushroom toast, the beet salad, and the roasted brussel sprouts. There was a ginger butternut squash amuse bouche brought out that I wished was on the menu because I would have a lot more of it. The entrees were the sea bass and the short ribs. Both, again, were out of this world. I ate every single bite. The dessert we shared was the carrot cake, and again I ate the whole entire thing. I was a big fatty by the end of the meal and I don't regret it one bit. They made a great old fashioned, one of the better ones in the city. Our server was sweet and friendly and very attentive. The next time I have a fancy pants dinner in mind and/or want to rock the socks off of a fellow foodie, I will come here in an instant.

text: 12/22/2012 Tonight hubby and I joined another couple for, sadly, the last night ever for Boxwood Bistro. The restaurant has been purchased, and will re-open roughly the third week in January under new ownership, new concept, etc. We have enjoyed many great meals there, and I've taken many friends who also enjoyed the casual elegance and great food offered. We had a chance on this last visit to chat with the incoming new owner, and I've got to say - I like him. Super nice guy that, seriously, went to work at BB as a bartender for a couple of months while contemplating buying the place (a' la Undercover Boss) to make sure this was the place. He's been in NYC, and LA, and is now wanting to put down roots in gool ol' Franklin, TN - and loved the charm of the place. So join me there next month, and let's all see what he has planned, OK? Prior review... Our "go to" spot for special occassion dinners (birthday, anniversary, or just celebrating life). We are treated like regulars, which is a great feeling in this day and age, even though I'd say we only visit maybe once every six weeks. The menu is quite good, only once in more than a dozen visits have we been disappointed with anything - and upon the server noticing our neglect of the ribs, they immediately replaced with another entree comping all for hubby's selections. This is one of those neighborhood places where you should feel like you are from the neighborhood, and if you don't like the location where you are seated (main room is noisy with wood floors, back room has carpet and is much quieter), then let them know. They are family-and-friends-owned and happy to accommodate any request - you just can't be shy. Their shrimp and grits are as good as any I've tried (not a spice fan, so if your basis is in that regard I can't comment). Their lunches are very nice and they're a great choice for Valentine's Day, etc. if you didn't reserve a year ahead. If shrimp bisque is the soup of the day, order it and you'll thank me later. Like others, I'm addicted to the strawberry cake, too. I've been known to order a whole one for a special birthday. I have also held a private event in their back room for my company, and the service and overall evening went very well.

text: It all started out fine. We were moving from Home 1 to Home 2. We wanted onsite storage like PODs that we could load at our convenience and then move to Home 2. I spoke with a nice enough guy in Nashville, David I think his name was. He told me all about the services and we agreed on a plan for my storage and moving needs. They would deliver a container (like a POD) to my home. We'd load it up at our convenience and then call them to pick it up and haul it to their conditioned storage facility. The initial delivery was done on time. The local company communicated well and I was pleased. From that moment on, the company became uncommunicative and unprofessional. The unit was picked up at Home 1 a day after we asked and without communication. It wasn't gone the day we expected, no one told us why. It was gone the next day. Okay. Skip to Home 2. We're ready to unload our storage unit. We scheduled to have it delivered on Wednesday so we're ready to unload for the weekend. Wednesday, nothing. Thursday, we call and leave a message. No response. Friday, we call and leave a message and email. The local operations manager calls back and explains that the driver was sick and they will get the unit to us on Monday. So we can't unload when we planned over the weekend. We were understanding, though it would be nice to be told this ahead of time. The unit doesn't show up until Tuesday. Not good. Skip to the end. We empty the storage unit the next weekend and email and call the company to come and pick up the unit. No response. Over the next TWO MONTHS, we make 10+ phone calls to the local franchise (no response) and the corporate office (1-800-PACK-RAT) and send numerous emails. Corporate says they'll make sure and take care of it. Over and over, nothing happens. The unit finally disappears 2 months after our initial request to have it picked up. Unless you want your yard to become a free advertising space for a 1-800-PACK-RAT billboard for an indefinite period of time, please don't give this company your business. They claim a 100% Satisfaction Guarantee. I couldn't be more dissatisfied.

Needless to say, I was touched when my boyfriend presented me with my own white orchid for Valentine's Day. It was one of the most thoughtful, lovely gifts I've ever received. Since it was purchased from Pure, I decided to pop in to get some tips for how to take care of my new beauty. The store had several interesting flowers and not the typical bouquets one would expect from a flower shop. The woman I spoke with was super helpful, and I'm so happy I stopped in. Apparently, orchids draw most of their moisture from the air, so it's really only necessary to water them about once a month with a half cup of hot water. Just cutting into it I needed something much more potent than the pathetic dinner knife I was provided. I needed a chainsaw or a radial saw, something with industrial strength and razor sharp blades. Then there was the issue of chewing this piece of mass produced biohazardous waste. I chomped with all my might and this piece of food was like a chunk out of a car tire. My teeth were no match. The sauce was just greasy cholesterol sludge that could have lubricated the pistons on a tractor trailer. Once it hit my stomach the indigestion began almost immediately. My belly became a churning washing machine. I highly recommend this place for when you are under the influence of powerful narcotics. The kind that numb the senses and neutralize the brain. Deep in the delusional caverns of imagination produced by such intoxication this assembly line slop can perhaps, maybe, pass as Italian food.

text: My overwhelming feeling upon visiting this place is sadness. Sadness that places like this have to exist and that extremely intelligent animals like chimps and orangutans have to live out there lives in small cement and bar cages. I have driven by this places at least a dozen times and never realized it was there until we sought it out after I purchased a Groupon. The place isn't very large- it took us just over an hour and that was walking slowly and taking our time. There are lots of volunteers hosing out cages, dishing out food, etc. There was one lady sitting with a pot belly pig. Another boy, only 9 years old, was in charge of a baby alligator. There are several types of apes, monkeys, lemurs and parrots. Each cage has a little sign telling you about the species inside. You can buy a small bag of food for $1. Most of the animals could care less about the food. The only animal that acted interested were the ducks. The goats would have been, but we couldn't really get to their enclosure. Some of the cages have pulley systems with cups or PVC pipes that allow you to slide food into the cages. It was moderately fun, my four year old enjoyed it for about 30 minutes. I'd wear closed toe shoes as there is a lot of dirt and fire ants. Some of the sanctuary is nicely shaded with cute little decor, other parts are in the blazing heat with stuff that is run down and in disrepair. I know money must be tight and I would hope any money they do have would go to the animals. But most of the cages are so barren and many of the animals look depressed. Especially the orangutan. Check out his sad eyes in the picture I took. The chimps too seemed sad- for such social animals many are kept isolated alone in cement cages. I'm sure there is a good reason why they are kept this way, and maybe they get some social interaction behind the scenes. This is where Cheetah (of Tarzan fame) lived, until he passed away recently. How sad that apes have been used in this way and this is the way they must spend the rest of their lives. I wish I was wealthy enough to build them something better! At least by going we helped to support the sanctuary in some small way. I'm sure there are many, many volunteers who love the animals and they are doing the best they can. It is still such a sad place.

text: Where do I start, I used to think of a hospital as a cold sterile place that people with a serious illness went to to get better or where pregnant women went rushing to have a baby delivered. I now know that a hospital can be allot more then just a place people go when they are sick. It can be a place that cares for its patients deeply, and sees them through one of the roughest and scariest times in their lives. We recently went through a crazy amount of months finding out we were having twins. Needless to say that makes allot of things fly around in your head about all the things that can go wrong. I was amazed at all the free classes they offer at Mercy to help new parents and people having twins. I will say that no class will ever ever prepare you for having twins. My wife was on bed-rest for about a week at home when she went to her OBGYN and she said she would not be working anymore. She got checked into the Anti-partum section of the hospital. I personally never even knew this area existed until I went to the multiples class at Mercy. Me and my wife kept thinking that bed-rest wouldn't happen to us but when it did I think it was the best thing for my wife. They took really good care of her and actually kept her busy doing crafts and other things with the other bed-rest moms. There was a lady named Amy that was really incredible, I think most people would think that she is a little to intense and hyper but I think that she really kept my wife and the other moms from getting down and loosing their minds. Through out the seven weeks she was on bed rest we only had a couple of times when issues came up that we didn't like but it wasn't anything to bad just mainly misunderstandings. I think back to how much my wife wanted to have our babies delivered a certain way and how much it didn't follow that path. I felt the entire time through out the delivery that the doctors knew exactly what they were doing even when when they had to do a C-section. After they were born they were whisked away to the NICU and the nurse that was there when they were checked in was incredible. She explained everything and then explained it again when my wife was out of surgery and came up to see the babies. I would have to say that the NICU staff was pretty incredible. I think that everything they could do they did. I really feel like they tried to connect with us every time we came up to visit which was every day for my wife. I really enjoyed the classes to help us make the twins coming home a better experience but the CPR classes really didn't give us warm and fuzzes, but I think it was a necessary step to take and was incredible that they offered it for free. All together I think very highly of Mercy hospital even the ER which is a sticking point for most people. I think people who call this hospital "The Baby Factory" think that is some kind of insult, but I think of it as a compliment. I would never take my wife to a hospital to deliver her babies at a hospital that didn't know what they were doing. I think if you deliver that many babies you Really know what you are doing. I also feel that the people that work in this hospital truly care for each and every person that comes through and that is not common. Thanks Mercy hospital for giving us the best experience life was willing to give us.
label: POS

text: Everyone who likes to spend under $30 for a pedicure will typically have their favorite hole-in-the-wall spot to go. For years I was loyal to a place not too far from my house (comparatively, since I live in North Marana) because they were competent... and close. My friend introduced me to Campbell Spa about a year and a half ago. Campbell (north of Grant, east side of street, in same strip as Blackjack pizza) was quite a long trip for me from home, and it isn't exactly convenient from my place of work either, so I thought this might be a one-time trip for the sake of hanging out with a friend. First thing that surprised me? The price. $20 for a pedicure is a good price. But when you find out that includes a free design... that's a GREAT price. You heard me. One free design on each big toe. Most other places would charge you $30-32 for the same services together. But for $20, they have to do a cheap job, right? On the contrary! These folks are good. Not the best, but for the price, very very good. Staff is friendly, and remembers you from when you've been there in the past. They've got the standard massage chairs, and plenty of great staff. When we got there, they told us our table wasn't quite ready and directed us to the bar to wait. Well about 20-25 minutes later we were seated. We ordered drinks (which in my opinion were a bit over priced..$16 for a glass of wine that cost about $25 a bottle). Then we ordered our appetizers. After about 20 or so minutes or apps came out. The apps were really good. I had the carpacio, and the rest of the table had the crab bisque and the baked shrimp. All were very good. After our apps, we ordered the meal and thats were our experience went way downhill. I ordered the 14oz filet medium rare. The rest of the table had a NY Strip (medium), and two delmonico steaks( one medium rare and one medium well). For sides we got the "table" size sides. We ordered the onion rings, steak fries, creamed spinach, and asparagus. We waited for at least 30 minutes before the waiter brought us some bread. about 10 minutes after the bread we finally got our food. My steak, I have to say, was perfect and very very good. (should be for a $60 steak). The two medium well steaks were cooked medium rare. Neither person who got the delmonico steaks were impressed and my wife hardly touched hers. The strip was good but under cooked and went half eaten. Now to the sides. They were the worst side dishes I have ever had in my life. The creamed spinach tasted like eggnog. It had way too much cream and nutmeg in it. It was horrible. The onion rings were OK. The steak fries were actually the worst I have ever had. They would have been better getting their fries from McDonalds. The fries were actually a whole potato that was cut in fours length wise and then fried. They were flavor less, over cooked and so dry we could barely choke them down. The asparagus was grilled and charred but sort of edible. They didn't season them at all with oil or salt and pepper before grilling. The biggest thing about the appetizers was the size. We all ordered the "table" size apps and the size was laughable. The onion rings had about 6 rings. The spinach arrived in a small appetizer boat. The steak fries had 6 fries and we got about 6 asparagus spears. Each person at the table got one onion ring, one fry, one asparagus spear and a small dollop of spinach. There was one of each app left on the plate after everyone got one. I don't know who thinks this is a portion enough for a table of four but the portions of each app were barely enough for one. We were actually laughing about it at the table. We debated ordering the "table" size chocolate cake dessert for $25 but decided against it as we figured that the "table" size of the cake was probably just a standard sized piece that they would cut into slivers at the table. Other than my filet, almost everything else was either just OK to downright awful. I expected much more from a $350 meal. I was very disappointed with Chophouse and I will never go back there again. If you want an extremely good and always consistent steakhouse, just go to Dickie Brennan's.

text: 1. Unique 2. Historical 3. Romantic = JACKPOT! New Orleans is divided into 72 different neighborhoods. Of those neighborhoods only one has really captured my heart in so many ways. The Vieux Carre (French Quarter) is, by far, my favorite neighborhood. We spend a lot of time together and I really can't live too happily without her. Resembling the Place des Vosges in Paris, Jackson Square is the heart of the French Quarter. It really is the spot in the Quarter that keeps this area alive. Bourbon Street may get the crowds but without Jackson Square this historic neighborhood would definitely not be the same. Jackson Square is a unique, historical, and memorable spot in the city. It is unique in that it is a park surrounded by a cathedral, shops, apartments, and restaurants. It is also known for all the street performers, musicians, and artists that set up shop there. Historically it was originally designed as a military parade ground. The three main buildings that surround Jackson Square all are historic landmarks: The St Louis Cathedral, the Presbytere, and the Cabildo. Lastly, there is not a more romantic spot than Jackson Square. The picturesque setting, the carriages, the weddings at the cathedral all contribute to the romance found here. There is no other place in the US quite like the French Quarter. Come here and experience a different way of life. I write this review today in honor of one of New Orleans iconic figures: Archbishop Philip Hannah. What a great man he was!! He led the Archdiocese of New Orleans for over two decades and today the St. Louis Cathedral is where Archbishop Hannah will be laid to rest. Jackson Square will be filled today with loving admirers witnessing a very memorable day today.

The various cooks in the back will usually chat with you about what they're making and it's really cool to see all the amazing food being prepared. What I really love though is the food. The general tso's dumplings are delicous and you just can't beat the various skewers. My favorite though are the brussels sprouts. text: I'm shocked and appalled that this place has 4 stars... and is even being compared to incredible places like Bibo's and The Hub. YUCK! Overall, I can honestly say this was probably the worst experience I've ever had at a coffee shop.... and I drink A LOT of coffee. Both in taste and customer service. This place would be a great place to put on Restaurant Impossible- where that guy comes in and changes everything! My husband and I enjoy going to local coffee shops in the mornings and reading and hanging out, and we'd never been to Hi Point, so we went this morning we decided to try it out, mostly because we had a Groupon and its right near our house, and man was I disappointed. We came in, and the guy (who I found out is one of the owners!) just stared at us, didn't say good morning, just stared. So we took a couple minutes and looked at the chalkboard of typical drinks behind the bar, and the whole time, he's not greeting us, or asking questions or anything? So I say, "We've never been in before, and we wanted to check it out this morning." He rudely replies, "Oh, great, what do you want to drink." And it wasn't like there was a big line, there were like 4 people in the whole place and no one in line. You'd think if someone had NEVER been in your place before and you clearly weren't busy with other customers, you'd take some time and welcome new customers and acclimate them to your establishment. Maybe give them some suggestions, or recommendations? No he just stood there staring. So I decided on a standard vanilla latte. And when I asked if they had to-go cups or if they had mugs to drink here, he was like, "Yes we have both," (like he was shocked that I even asked) so I said I'd like it for here and then I saw him pull out a pint glass.... Ok, if you're going to own a place with COFFEE In the title... BUY SOME COFFEE MUGS!!!!! I understand using pint glasses for iced drinks or toward the end of a busy day, when all your mugs need to be washed, but it was 6:30am.... at a coffee shop and they didn't have any coffee mugs? Anyways, I decided to request it be put in a to-go cup, because I'm not a huge fan of drinking hot coffee out of a pint glass. At this point he hasn't even acknowledged my husband or what he would like to drink. So he finished my latte and proceeds to ring me up separately, not even asking if my husband who I clearly came in with wants anything, or if we'd like anything to eat? So my husband also chimes that he'd also like a vanilla latte to go, and the guys was like, Oh, and proceeded to make my husbands drink too. ? And as he's doing that, I ask what something was in the glass pastry case. I said, what is that ball looking thing with all the sesame seeds on it. So he sets the milk down that's steaming and walks to the case, looks in, walks back to the milk and say, "Those are bagels!" Like I was an idiot for even asking! But it wasn't like they had holes in the middle, or even looked like bagels, they looked like a mound of dough with seasame seeds on it? So he finished my husbands drink, and started to ring us up again. He didn't say, would you like that bagel or something else to eat? So I went ahead and requested the bagel anyways, we had a $10 Groupon, so I figured we utilize all of it. Then we go and sit down and that's when I realize how ridiculous the decor is. I appreciate eclectic, but this was just messy. I really enjoy those places that have mis-matched antique tables and chairs when they're done correctly. All vintage, or all modern... this was just a hodge-podge of things they probably found at garage sales, some new some old, some matching some didn't. There was just no rhyme or reason to why they decorated the way they did. There were chairs turned upside down under the bar, which I presume is extra storage? It just looked bad and the floor (although probably just old) look disgustingly dirty. All of that aside, if the coffee would have been great, everything could have probably been overlooked- but the coffee and food were just as bad as the service! The coffee was stale tasting, there was zero vanilla flavor, and the OWNER clearly has no idea how to steam milk properly. When you make a latte, you add the espresso to the cup first and then lay the milk in nicely... he did it backward. Then the bagel that was toasted on a paninni grill, was hard, resembled and tasted like a firm hamburger bun and it was burned on one whole half of it. When we left, no one was even at the counter to say good bye or check and see how things were. Like I said at the beginning, this was the worst coffee experience I've had in a LONG time. If you're going to spend good money on a latte DON'T go to this place. Go to The Hub or Bibo's, (they're worth the drive to the center of town) or even Starbucks across the street is better than this! I usually enjoy supporting locals, but unfortunately, this is not a place I will support.

text: Yet another restaurant that is suffering as a result of being unable to handle a sudden influx of customers from Groupon. But here's the thing. THEY WERE NOT THAT BUSY.
