It's barbecue. Pretty simple and straightforward. So why did it take an hour and a half for food to appear in front of us? The only reason I didn't storm out of there much earlier is because my dining partner, Cherie O, is WAY nicer of a person than I am. The place is a little hole in the wall, and the atmosphere is actually pretty nice. Pub-like, but homey. The people were down-home and friendly. But that's where the positivity ends. First we were told by a server that there was a 20-25 minute wait, and gestured at the bar for us to wait. So we sat ourselves there and chatted amongst ourselves. About 15 minutes goes by, and another server comes by and asks for our order. I was taken aback and said, "There's no menu in front of us." She told me that it was on the chalkboard on the wall, but since we hadn't realized we were supposed to be looking at it (I thought we were on a wait!), she left us to decide, and disappeared for another 10 minutes. The menu is extremely small. No explanation of sides or anything. The server wasn't even sure what they had in stock. We couldn't see the chalkboard well from where we were sitting and kept having to get up and walk over there to look. I was annoyed by the lack of communication all around, here. Felt like the server tried to bully me into ordering things I didn' t want. Me: I'll just have a water. Her: Well, we have a, b, c... Me: I'll take the water. Her: *ignoring me* And we have x, y, z. ME: A WATER, PLEASE. Her. Okay. Really? And then after we ordered, nothing happened. I noticed that every other patron in the restaurant was visibly as annoyed as I was. People that had been there longer than we were had been receiving plates in an untimely manner as well. Slow, slow, slow, SLOW service. Unreasonably slow. One guy ended up going through a door and BEHIND the bar (much to the server's chagrin) because he couldn't get her attention to give them basic things, like napkins. I ended up going over and asking another server if he can make sure our orders are to go (I am very frustrated by this point and just want to leave, and was envisioning it taking an additional 20-30 minutes to get our checks and pay). He told us, "Well, they were just now plating your food, but we'll box it for you now"....but yet it took 15 minutes to come out to us (no, these time estimations are not exaggerated. I timed it). Then it came out from the original server on plates. I told her that we wanted it to go, and she was very frustrated that "no one told her that"....cue another 10 minutes before she brought it out in boxes for us. As soon as the food was in hand, I wanted to run out of the place as fast as possible. Also, we never received our drinks (a sweet tea and a water), and our server even pointed that out at the end, and told us we wouldn't be charged. But we didn't get an actual receipt, and didn't realize until on the way home that she charged us for the sweet tea anyway. Sigh. So I got home (only a five minute drive, btw, so it's not like the quality of the food was affected; it was still warm) and after all that waiting, the food wasn't good. The baked beans were definitely from a can, but they were the most palatable part of the meal. The french fries were way overseasoned with black pepper. The pulled pork I ordered was on Texas toast (prefer a bun), completely saturated in overly sweet barbecue sauce, with jalapenos on top. I couldn't taste the pork at all. Barbecue that has to hide behind all those other flavors is not high quality barbecue, as far as I'm concerned. I was starving, but I didn't finish my sandwich, because it was just not good. Very disappointed. If the food had been good, I would have been willing to give it another chance, especially considering the Groupon. But both bad food and bad service means I won't be going back.

text: I will join the chorus of the previous reviewers who praised the lunch prix fixe. There is, in my opinion, no better way to $20 in daylight hours in New Orleans. A note for out of town visitors: you will still be seated and will likely still receive excellent service if you arrive wearing shorts and a t-shirt, as did the gentlemen at the table near mine did today. You will, however, appear very much out of place. Proudly, most locals have resisted the encroachment of the pervasive casualness of American dining attire. To a New Orleanian, mid-90s temperatures will not excuse one from wearing a jacket to dinner. Whenever Chef Besh offers a charcuterie dish one would be wise to order it: the pate de campagne served with assorted marmalade, jam and mustard (and a pickled chantrelle!) on offer as a first course was excellent. The Mangalitsa pork belly, mustard greens, and creole cream cheese malfatti (think gnocci but swap the potato for creole cream cheese) was a fine balance of fat and lean, savory, bitter and sour. I really like the way the flavor of the dumpling worked with the mustard greens, one of those ingredients that always triggers a subconscious emotional response in me and perhaps others who grew up with greens growing in the backyard garden. Besh's lasting contribution to our cuisine is his ability to elevate such humble and utilitarian local ingredients seamlessly into a "fine dining" setting. And rightly so -- "fine" should be indicative of the skilled preparation and above all flavor of a dish, not the expensiveness or remote provenance of a dish's ingredients. I'm as impressed as the next guy with beluga caviar or pata negra jamon or whatever the show-off ingredient in vogue may be, but we have an abundance of fine ingredients in South Louisiana and Chef Besh showcases them with aplomb. (Don't try to fault me for inconsistency because I'll bet you that Mangalitsa was raised locally.) August is no doubt deserving of the consistent high praise it receives as being among the best restaurants in New Orleans.

The new food menu isn't cheap, but not too pricy: value enough for your money. I recommend the salads. The pizza is still thin and crispy. But there it is. For the experience, its well priced. The ambiance makes this place, with mirrors lining the walls, white linen table clothes, chandeliers: class, class, class! Dinner was pretty tasty, as were our drinks. I'm smitten that we found this gem.
label: POS

text: I went to Engima this morning for the first time, to use my Buy With Me voucher for a 50-minute facial. Overall, it was a good experience but not great. Let's start with the pros: the interior is nice, so you kind of forget you're in a strip mall; the woman who did the computerized skin analysis seemed knowledgeable and gave good advice; the woman who did my facial also seemed knowledgeable and gave good recommendations. Now, the cons: the staff were not all that friendly (perhaps this is a Russian thing?); the facial did not turn out to be too relaxing due to the fact that the walls are super thin and don't reach to the ceiling, so you can hear people talking in the waiting area; the woman doing the facial did not talk to me about anything she was doing or using on my skin. She came at my face with a machine that sounded like a combination of an electric razor and a lazer. It felt like sandpaper as it zapped at my face. I would have liked to know what it was doing, or at least give me a little heads up before you zap me. Depending on how their regular prices compare to other area spas, I'd probably return for another facial.
label: POS
